title: Tunisian honeycomb cushion cover
excerpt: A textured cushion cover in aran yarn using Tunisian honeycomb stitch. The offset stitch pattern creates raised cells that mimic the look of a honeycomb without cables.
sourceNotes: Tunisian honeycomb stitch alternates simple and extended stitches in a staggered arrangement to produce a three-dimensional cell pattern.

glossaryTerms.definition: A Tunisian pattern that alternates simple stitches with extended stitches in a brick-like offset arrangement. The extended stitches push forward to form raised cells.
Like the simple stitch but with an extra yarn-over worked before pulling through the loop on the hook. This adds height to the stitch and creates textured pockets.
A pattern where the stitches in alternate rows shift by half a repeat width. The offset gives the honeycomb its cell-like appearance.
A simple way to close a cushion cover without a zip. Two overlapping panels on the back create an opening wide enough to insert a cushion pad.

crochet.gaugeText: 14 sts x 13 rows = 10 x 10 cm in Tunisian honeycomb stitch.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Approx. 45 x 45 cm to fit a standard 45 cm cushion pad.

14 sts x 13 rows = 10 x 10 cm in Tunisian honeycomb stitch.

Row 1 forward pass: (1 simple st, 1 extended st) repeat across. Row 2 forward pass: (1 extended st, 1 simple st) repeat across. All return passes: ch 1, (yo, pull through 2 loops) across. Repeat rows 1 and 2 throughout.
Chain 64. Work in honeycomb stitch for 58 rows (approx. 45 cm). Fasten off.
Chain 64. Work in Tunisian simple stitch for 32 rows (approx. 25 cm). Fasten off. Overlap the two back panels by 10 cm and tack lightly to hold for assembly.
Place the front and overlapped back panels together, wrong sides out. Join all four edges with a flat slip stitch seam. Turn right side out. Insert the cushion pad through the envelope opening.
Weave in all ends with the tapestry needle.
